title: House of Bourbon
capsule: The House of Bourbon originated as lords of Bourbon-l'Archambault in the Bourbonnais, with the connection to the Capetian royal house established through Robert of Clermont, sixth son of Louis IX, who married Beatrice of Burgundy in 1272. The duchy was erected for Louis I in 1327, and under Constable Charles III of Bourbon the family reached its apogee before his defection to Charles V in 1523 led to attainder and confiscation of Bourbon lands in 1527. The Vendôme branch survived; Henry of Navarre, descended from Louis I, inherited the French throne in 1589 as Henry IV, inaugurating the Bourbon monarchy that would rule France until 1792 and again from 1814 to 1830.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Bourbon lordship and duchy is well documented from French royal and seigneurial records, though borders shifted repeatedly through inheritance and confiscation.
